title: Give functions one reason to change
body: A focused function is easier to name, test, reuse, and replace.
takeaway: If a function needs and then in its name, consider splitting it.

title: Name the intent
body: Which variable name best communicates a duration measured in milliseconds?
takeaway: Names should carry meaning and units when ambiguity is costly.

title: Make failure explicit
body: A result type can represent success or a known failure without exceptions for expected outcomes.
takeaway: Model recoverable failure as data the caller must handle.

title: Bound remote work
body: Network calls should not wait forever.
takeaway: Set a timeout and define what the user sees when it expires.

title: Retry with restraint
body: Which failure is usually safe to retry with backoff?
takeaway: Retry transient failures, not permanent input or authorization errors.

title: Validate at the boundary
body: Check external data when it enters your system, then let internal code rely on stronger guarantees.
takeaway: Parse once into a valid domain type instead of checking everywhere.

title: Why does the set contain duplicates?
body: Two objects represent the same user but the set keeps both. What is missing?
takeaway: Equality and hashCode must describe the same identity.

title: Cancel stale work
body: Search results from an older query should not overwrite a newer query.
takeaway: Cancel stale requests or compare request tokens before applying results.

title: Write useful logs
body: Which log is most useful during an incident?
takeaway: Structured context makes failures searchable and actionable.

title: Why is the wrong result cached?
body: Responses vary by locale, but the cache key contains only the URL. What is wrong?
takeaway: A cache key must include every input that can change the output.
